root_cause.text: The use of `init_waitqueue_entry` (which does not clear list pointers) combined with a conditional `remove_wait_queue` that is skipped when the substream is concurrently unlinked leaves the wait entry orphaned on the old sleep queue, causing list corruption when the entry is later added to a new queue.
root_cause.evidence: "init_waitqueue_entry which does not clear entry.prev/next, and add_wait_queue with a conditional remove_wait_queue that is skipped when to_check is no longer in the group after concurrent UNLINK. The orphaned wait entry remains on the unlinked substream sleep queue. On the next drain iteration, add_wait_queue adds the entry to a new queue while still linked on the old one, corrupting both lists."
